messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: warmup failures detected for pool-us-east-2-dedicated (model: rdw-model-v2-7b). 120 failures in last 2m, error mix: OOM at load, deserialization errors, compile timeouts. Routing degraded for some Dedicated customers.

nate (infra): seeing the same in infra logs. kube events show repeated pod CrashLoopBackOff during init. suggests OOM during model deserialization. attaching recent pod log snippet.
```
[init] loading weights rdw-model-v2-7b
error: runtime: out of memory allocating 0x1c000000
panic: runtime error: memory exhausted
```

lee (runtime): compile step also timing out for a subset of models. logs from compile worker:
```
compile-worker: compiling kernels for rdw-model-v2-7b, seq_len=2048
timeout after 120s waiting for kernel JIT
error: compile timeout
```

olivia (sre): impact estimate? any customer facing errors/latency spikes reported?

maria (support): CS ticket #4567 opened by AcmeCorp complaining about request errors (500) and some token-level delays. They are on Dedicated in us-east-2 and pinned to v2-7b.

carmen (oncall): I'm taking this. o11y: can we get a quick count of affected hosts and number of active customers on that pool? nate, lee — can you triage warmup path? I'll coordinate pages and customer comms.

nate (infra): affected hosts: 7 of 22 GPUs in pool showing repeated OOM during warmup. Active pinned contracts: 3 customers, ~200 req/s of routed traffic. Moving traffic off the pool now to minimize customer impact.

pagerduty-bot: Paging carmen (oncall) — incident assigned. Severity P1. Handoff window 15m.

lee (runtime): quick hypothesis: recent kernel selection change bumped memory working set for JITed kernels + our deserialization path isn't streaming weights (we allocate full tensor upfront). For large 7B weights that's crossing available reserved memory and causing OOM. Also some models hit an uncommon codepath that falls back to a slower compile routine which exceeds 120s timeout.

carmen (oncall): mitigation plan 1) stop warmups on new pods, 2) route traffic to compatible smaller model variant (v2-7b-quant or v2-3b) if available, 3) attempt manual load with streaming deserialization on a non-prod node to validate.

lee (runtime): implementing a conservative warmup flag now to use streaming deserialize and skip heavy JIT for warmup. pushing config to canary host.

nate (infra): moved routing: -30% traffic to fallback models, draining new pods from pool-us-east-2-dedicated. creating ephemeral hosts to absorb active sessions.

maria (support): notifying AcmeCorp: "We are aware of 500s for some requests in us-east-2 and routing traffic to a compatible model variant while we fix warmup issues. ETA 30-60m. Will update in 10m." :phone:

lee (runtime): manual warmup test results on canary host:
```
warmup --model rdw-model-v2-7b --stream-weights
deser: streamed ok, peak mem 42GB
compile: skipped heavy JIT; using precompiled kernels fallback
result: load SUCCESS (took 38s)
```

olivia (sre): good. can we push streaming-deserialize as immediate mitigator to the remaining hosts in the pool? also, lower compile timeout to 90s for now to fail-fast and avoid long hangs.

nate (infra): rolling streaming-deserialize config to remaining 15 hosts in pool (gradual 3-host batches). lowering compile timeout via runtime-config map now.

lee (runtime): note: streaming-deserialize reduces peak mem by ~20% but increases load time slightly. acceptable trade for stability. implementing a follow-up to add retry-on-deser-failure.

carmen (oncall): customer comms updated. monitoring error rate and latency. if stable for 10m we'll start reintroducing traffic. tagging this as P1 — investigating root cause deeper after stabilization.

olivia (sre): observed error rate drop from 6% -> 0.6% in last 5m after Traffic shift + streaming-deser. latency normalized for fallback routes.

maria (support): AcmeCorp confirmed improvement and reduced errors. asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

lee (runtime): temporary mitigation summary: streaming weights + use precompiled kernel fallback for warmup + lower compile timeout. suspect regression in kernel selection memory footprint introduced in last runtime build (runt-2026-03-12).

carmen (oncall): next steps/action items:
- lee: revert or patch kernel selection to reduce mem OR add auto-quant path for warmup (owner: lee, ETA 3d)
- nate: increase compile cache and prefetch artifacts for common models (owner: nate, ETA 2d)
- infra+devex: add warmup health checks and deserialization retries (owner: infra/devex, ETA 5d)
- ops: prepare runbook update for similar warmup OOM events (owner: carmen, ETA 1d)

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated. Assigned to carmen (oncall).

carmen (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for customer impact. keeping thread open for root cause work and postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:

lee (runtime): will collect compile logs and create a repro on staging. scheduling follow-up meeting with kernel team.

olivia (sre): reopening if errors reoccur. otherwise please file postmortem with timeline and include diagnostics (heap profiles, compile traces). thanks team.

maria (support): I'll close CS ticket after postmortem link added and customer confirmed final resolution.
